newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine business optimistic for 1997 - survey.
newsitem.headline: Argentine business optimistic for 1997 - survey.

text.p: A monthly survey of Argentine businesses shows that two out of three companies expect activity to pick up next year, the Economy Ministry said on Monday.
"The poll for 1997 confirms the rebound seen in the third and fourth quarters," the ministry said in a release.

Asked about the outlook for their businesses, 64.3 percent of the companies surveyed said they expected an improvement, 32.1 percent saw no change and 3.6 percent thought next year would be worse than 1996.

Some 58.9 percent of the companies polled said their exports should rise in the coming year, 19.6 percent saw exports falling and 12.5 percent expected no change. Of the remaining nine percent that currently do not export goods, 70 percent said they expected to start exporting in 1997.
About 54 percent of those polled intend to increase investments on their plants next year, 3.5 percent expect to cut investments and 42 percent saw no change.
The ministry did not say how many companies responded to the survey.
